item.title: A VQE simulation of the transverse field Ising model
item.description: arXiv:2611.05379v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: One of the most promising applications of quantum computing is the ability to simulate quantum systems. A quantity of particular importance in condensed matter physics is the ground-state energy of a system. Here, we present an implementation of a hybrid quantum-classical algorithm known as the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) to estimate the ground state energy of a prototypical quantum spin system. For this spin system, we use the transverse field Ising model (TFIM) which is known to exhibit a quantum phase transition (QPT) at a critical point. We apply the VQE to a $4$-spin TFIM and evaluate its performance using both a local noise model and IBM quantum hardware to estimate the ground-state energy and reproduce the QPT. The resulting ground-state energy estimates and QPT behaviour are compared with exact-diagonalisation benchmarks.
item.dc:creator: Luke Bennett

item.title: Exact chiral symmetry, non-Hermiticity, and the axial anomaly on the lattice: A symmetry-class criterion for disorder-induced undoubling
item.description: arXiv:2611.05395v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A lattice Dirac operator designed to preserve exact chiral symmetry by weighting the derivative with a quenched random field---the \emph{chiral disordered fermions} (\CDF) of [L.\ Jacobs, Phys.\ Rev.\ Lett.\ \textbf{51}, 172 (1983)]---is reexamined with modern tools. We show that the disorder-averaged operator satisfies $\anticomm{\Deff}{\gfive}=0$ exactly, to all orders in disorder strength. Disorder lifts the doubler degeneracy, driving doublers off the real axis into a complex mass while the physical mode remains protected, but does so through non-Hermiticity rather than a Ginsparg--Wilson relation. Consequently the axial index vanishes in every formulation: the Hermitian trace $\Tr(\gfive D)$, the bi-orthogonal index for non-Hermitian operators, and the algebraic Riesz-projector index, including at exceptional points. The \CDF operator therefore cannot reproduce the axial anomaly: its failure is enforced by the exact chiral symmetry it preserves. We classify neighboring constructions by the Dirac channel carrying the lattice structure. Disorder in the $\g_\mu$ channel preserves chirality, realizes an Altland--Zirnbauer chiral class, and cannot carry an index; disorder in the $\mathbb{1}$ mass channel breaks chiral symmetry and yields Callan--Harvey/domain-wall physics. A one-parameter family interpolates between them, with the 1983 operator and Kaplan's domain wall as opposite limits, distinguished not by disorder itself but by the channel it occupies. This unifies lattice-QCD undoubling with the tenfold-way classification of disordered Dirac fermions and settles the disorder route to chiral lattice fermions.
item.dc:creator: Laurence A. Jacobs

item.title: Worm Algorithms for the Schwinger Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.05402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This thesis studies the Schwinger model in (1 + 1) dimensions using a lattice formulation and its dual representation. The model provides a simple yet non-trivial setting for investigating characteristic phenomena of gauge theories, including screening, confinement-related behaviour, the Schwinger effect and dependence on the topological angle ($\theta$). After introducing the Euclidean formulation with staggered fermions, we describe the dual transformation in which the original degrees of freedom are replaced by configurations of plaquettes, dimers and, in the massive case, monomers. The main objective is to investigate the numerical behaviour of the model in the presence of a fermion mass and a topological angle. We implement Monte Carlo algorithms adapted to the dual representation, including local and non-local updates that allow admissible configurations to be sampled. For the massive model, we also analyse the emergence of the sign problem and its effect on the estimation of observables through reweighting. From the simulations we compute several quantities, including the average plaquette, the dimer density, the chiral condensate and the average sign. These observables characterise the dependence on the mass, coupling and topological angle ($\theta$), and identify the regions in which the sign problem becomes most significant. Finally, we discuss the numerical results and the usefulness of the dual formulation for investigating gauge theories in non-perturbative regimes.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Ram\'irez Zalduendo

item.title: Finite-volume Analysis of On-shell Subtraction in the Luescher formalism
item.description: arXiv:2611.05899v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On-shell subtraction is a relevant step in finite-volume analyses, which is to isolate an on-shell singularity and evaluate regular momentum-dependent factors at their on-shell values. For short-range interactions with a finite mass gap, the correction associated with this on-shell subtraction is exponentially suppressed at sufficiently large volume and can therefore be neglected at the corresponding accuracy. We examine how this correction changes as the relevant mass parameter decreases. Using a common dimensional-regularization prescription, we derive analytic expressions for the resulting finite volume correction for representative momentum structures and examine their behavior numerically. For a nonzero mass parameter, the corrections are indeed exponentially suppressed at large $\mu L$, whereas in the massless limit this suppression is replaced by an enhanced finite-volume dependence. More importantly, the $S$-wave contribution can develop an infrared divergence of finite volume correction in the massless limit. These results clarify the conditions under which on-shell subtraction can be applied and provide guidance for assessing such corrections in finite-volume hadronic calculations involving long-range effects, including QCD+QED.
item.dc:creator: Wanchen Lei, Yuting Wang, Jin-Yi Pang

item.title: Quantum Computing for Entanglement Asymmetry and the Quantum Mpemba Effect in Field Theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.05987v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a quantum measurement protocol for estimating the R\'enyi entanglement asymmetry, which quantifies symmetry breaking at the level of a subsystem and provides a probe of the quantum Mpemba effect. The protocol combines the SWAP test with a charge-resolving procedure based on randomized symmetry rotations. For a fixed additive accuracy $\epsilon$, the required number of measurements scales as $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-2})$ without explicit dependence on the total system size, making the protocol particularly attractive for quantum many-body systems and lattice quantum field theories. As a representative application, we study the quantum Mpemba effect in the lattice Schwinger model with a $\theta$ term using classical state-vector simulations. We further estimate the resources required to implement the protocol on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices, fault-tolerant quantum computers (FTQCs), and a representative early-FTQC architecture. Our results provide a measurement-efficient framework for investigating anomalous symmetry-restoration dynamics in quantum many-body systems and quantum field theories.
item.dc:creator: Keisuke Fujii, Harunobu Fujimura, Masazumi Honda, Duc Truyen Le

item.title: Simulating a chiral gauge theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.06880v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chiral gauge theories underlie the Standard Model, yet none has been simulated nonperturbatively. Lattice constructions that evade the Nielsen-Ninomiya obstruction entail complex fermion measures or infinite-dimensional local Hilbert spaces. Here we provide a gauge-invariant Hamiltonian lattice regularization of 1+1-dimensional abelian chiral gauge theories built from clock-and-shift qudits with $\mathbb{Z}_N$ gauge fields, in which the global chiral symmetry and its 't Hooft anomaly survive exactly mod $N$. Anomaly cancellation on the lattice lets the Gauss laws be imposed and solved exactly, reducing the theory to an unconstrained qudit chain. Using infinite matrix product states, we simulate the canonical 1+1-dimensional chiral gauge theory, the 34-50 model, and find excellent agreement with analytic predictions, showing that a finite-dimensional local Hilbert space at $N=6$ reproduces the expected infrared physics of the continuum 34-50 model. This provides an efficient and practical solution to the problem of simulating general abelian chiral gauge theories in 1+1 dimensions, both on classical and quantum computers.
item.dc:creator: Laurens Lootens, Hersh Singh

item.title: Quantum computing for high energy nuclear physics
item.description: arXiv:2611.05491v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum information science (QIS) offers a new set of conceptual and computational tools ideally suited to exploring the many-body, out-of-equilibrium, and real-time properties of strongly interacting quantum systems. These themes find a natural counterpart in high energy nuclear physics, whose central goal is to describe the properties of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD), the theory of the strong interaction, under extreme conditions. Relevant examples range from the formation and internal structure of hadrons, to the collective and thermalization dynamics of strongly interacting QCD matter, and the properties of complex many-body scattering processes. Although tremendous progress has been made over the past decades in our understanding of QCD in the nuclear physics context, through perturbative methods, lattice QCD, and effective theory descriptions, phenomena that are intrinsically connected to real-time dynamics, highly entangled many-body evolution, or finite density regimes remain only partially accessible with existing approaches. In this article, we argue that QIS can help realize a new paradigm for addressing these open questions. With the aim of making the discussion accessible to both high energy nuclear physics and QIS audiences, we provide an overview of selected open problems in high energy nuclear physics, with emphasis on aspects motivated by collider phenomenology, and discuss how they can be approached using QIS tools. This connection is illustrated through representative examples drawn from the recent literature, making the case that QIS can become a driving force for discovery in nuclear physics in the coming years.
item.dc:creator: Jo\~{a}o Barata

item.title: Proton generalized parton distributions from electromagnetic form factors: A theoretically constrained phenomenological reconstruction
item.description: arXiv:2611.05635v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a theoretically constrained phenomenological reconstruction of the unpolarized, chiral-even, leading-twist proton generalized parton distributions $H^q$ and $E^q$. At zero skewness, valence-quark distributions are combined with flavor-dependent exponential profiles calibrated simultaneously against phenomenological representations of the proton and neutron electromagnetic form factors. The construction imposes exact valence and anomalous-magnetic-moment normalizations, the low-scale condition $B^{u+d}(0)=0$, the required endpoint behavior, and the complete Gaussian impact-parameter positivity bound. The resulting parametrization provides a reasonable description of the electromagnetic form factors and their slopes while revealing the tension between strict GPD consistency and a precision reproduction of all low-$Q^2$ observables within the adopted ansatz. We extend the distributions to nonzero skewness using normalized double distributions and introduce an independent $D$-term to complete the relevant Mellin polynomials. We examine electromagnetic and energy--momentum-tensor form factors, impact-parameter distributions, positivity, polynomiality, and illustrative mechanical properties. The analysis distinguishes information constrained by electromagnetic data from additional assumptions governing skewness and the mechanical sector, thereby providing a transparent elastic baseline for future studies of nucleon-to-resonance transition GPDs.
item.dc:creator: A. Capelo-Astudillo, T. Aguilar, M. Conde-Correa, A. Duenas-Vidal, P. G. Ortega, J. Segovia

item.title: Statistical mechanics and hierarchy of learnability in quantum codes: From generalized symmetries to non-Abelian topological orders
item.description: arXiv:2611.06154v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Local weak measurements provide noisy information about observables encoded in a quantum code. We formulate the corresponding Bayesian inference problem for a broad class of topological stabilizer codes by mapping it to classical spin models with generalized symmetries. When the wavefunction deformation and Gaussian measurement strengths coincide, the replicated model acquires an enlarged symmetry. We use this symmetry to derive exact identities among correlators averaged over measurement records that quantify the learnability of nonlocal observables associated with fractionalized excitations. Together with correlation inequalities in the associated clean ferromagnetic models, these identities establish hierarchies of learnability: if two observables remain learnable at long distances, their product must also remain learnable. We demonstrate these relations in the rank-2 toric code and the X-cube model, whose classical descriptions exhibit modulated and subsystem symmetries, respectively. We further extend the analysis to finite group quantum double models, including non-Abelian ones. We derive exact relations between learnability and correlations in the corresponding classical models, and show that the representation structure and fusion rules of anyons impose further constraints under suitable positivity conditions. These results constrain which types of nonlocal information can be learned simultaneously, providing a guide to learning phase diagrams in quantum codes under local weak measurements.
item.dc:creator: Hiromi Ebisu, Masazumi Honda

item.title: A Duality Model in Which Dual QCD Becomes Hydrodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.06503v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Revisiting a duality model in which dual QCD becomes hydrodynamics, or the dual gluon is a fluid, allows us to understand some of the mysteries of QCD, such as the behavior of the quark--gluon plasma (QGP) as a perfect fluid and gluon saturation in the structure function at high energies. This old-fashioned duality converts the gluon action into hydrodynamics described by the 2-form stream function $W^a_{\mu\nu}$ with eight colors. All interactions then become current--current interactions of the Nambu--Jona-Lasinio type. The resulting theory admits a strong-coupling expansion about the fluid. This can provide a third method to supplement perturbative QCD and lattice QCD.
item.dc:creator: Noriaki Aibara, So Katagiri, Yoshiki Matsuoka, Kazuya Mitsutani, Akio Sugamoto

item.title: Non-compact Kogut-Susskind gauge theories: 1D lattice models with exact ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ gauge invariance
item.description: arXiv:2611.06771v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Kogut-Susskind (KS) formulation of gauge theories constructs quantum many-body Hamiltonians with gauge invariance under a compact Lie group exactly implemented on a spatial lattice. Here, we revisit this construction for a non-compact gauge group. Although motivated in part by theories like general relativity whose first-order formulation involves the non-compact Lorentz group as a local symmetry, we focus on simpler cases in one spatial dimension akin to the Schwinger model. In a bottom-up approach, we show how exact gauge invariance under the simplest non-compact Lie group ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ can be retained exactly on a 1D lattice, and highlight the differences that arise with respect to compact gauge groups, including a continuous spectrum of the Casimir operators of the gauge fields and the emergence of infinite-dimensional representations of the matter fields. For the pure gauge theory, we discuss how a consistent restriction to the positive semigroup ${\rm SL}^{+}(2,\mathbb{R})$ reproduces well-known results from the quantization of Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) gravity. Motivated by the constraint structure of general dilaton gravity, we introduce static charges coupled to the non-compact gauge field, which can be realised by single-fermion degrees of freedom living in an additional, synthetic dimension. With static charges our lattice model remains exactly integrable, but when extending to dynamical fermionic matter, we arrive at an interacting 1D ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ KS gauge theory. We give an interpretation of this model as a chain of charges sequentially connected by strings whose tension pulls matter left or right depending on the sign of the relative continuous ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ fluxes. This picture becomes exact when the involved ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ charges are strongly self-interacting, where we solve the reduced two-body problem analytically.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Fulgado-Claudio, Torsten V. Zache

item.title: $\bar{D}$-meson Nucleon Scattering from Lattice QCD at the Physical Point
item.description: arXiv:2603.12251v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We report the first lattice QCD study of the $s$-wave scattering of the $\bar{D}$-meson and the nucleon at the physical point, utilizing (2+1)-flavor configurations generated by the HAL QCD collaboration with a pion mass of $m_\pi\simeq 137$ MeV and a lattice spacing of $a\simeq0.084$ fm. By applying the HAL QCD method to the four-point correlation function of the $\bar{D}N$ system, we obtain a leading-order potential of the derivative expansion of the interaction kernel, which is then used to extract the $s$-wave phase shifts of low-energy $\bar{D}N$ scattering. Both the isospin $I=0$ and $I=1$ channels have a short-range repulsive core and a shallow attractive pocket in the intermediate to long-range region, though the $I=0$ channel is more attractive than the $I=1$ channel. We also observe that the $\bar{D}N$ potential exhibits more attraction than the $KN$ potential, which is its analog in the strange sector. In terms of the $s$-wave phase shifts, the $I=0$ channel shows a weak attractive behavior in the low-energy region with a positive scattering length of $0.425 \pm 0.163 (_{-0.105}^{+0.129})$ fm, whereas the $I=1$ channel shows repulsion with a negative scattering length of $-0.235 \pm 0.046 (_{-0.007}^{+0.040})$ fm. No bound states are found in both isospin channels, indicating the absence of a pentaquark state in the $s$-wave $\bar{D}N$ system.
item.dc:creator: Wren Yamada, Yan Lyu, Kotaro Murakami, Takumi Doi

item.title: Scalable Generative Sampling and Multilevel Estimation for Lattice Field Theories Near Criticality
item.description: arXiv:2604.10209v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Sampling lattice field theories near criticality is severely hindered by critical slowing down, which makes standard Markov chain methods increasingly inefficient at large lattice volumes. We introduce a multiscale generative sampler, inspired by renormalization-group ideas, that models the Boltzmann distribution through a coarse-to-fine hierarchy across length scales. At each level, a conditional Gaussian mixture model captures the main local dependence of newly introduced variables on the already-sampled coarse field, while a masked continuous normalizing flow refines the remaining conditional structure. Coarse levels encode the dominant long-wavelength modes, and finer levels progressively add short-distance fluctuations. In addition, because the architecture preserves coarse fields exactly during refinement, it provides exact restriction maps at no additional computational cost and directly enables asymptotically unbiased Multilevel Monte Carlo (MLMC) variance reduction. For the two-dimensional scalar $\phi^4$ theory near criticality, the method achieves integrated autocorrelation times orders of magnitude smaller than Hybrid Monte Carlo (HMC) on large volumes, maintains high importance-sampling efficiency relative to other generative baselines, and reproduces asymptotically unbiased physical observables in statistical agreement with long HMC simulations.
item.dc:creator: Ankur Singha, Jacob Kauffmann, Elia Cellini, Karl Jansen, Shinichi Nakajima

item.title: Finite-volume effects on smeared spectral densities
item.description: arXiv:2606.14349v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Using two distinct approaches, we derive a universal expression for the leading finite-volume effects of the smeared vector-vector spectral density (proportional to the smeared hadronic $R$-ratio) in a periodic cubic spatial volume of side length $L$. First, building on the results of previous work for finite-volume effects on Euclidean two-point functions, we show that the $L$ dependence is exponentially suppressed for a certain class of smearing kernels, and that the leading effects can be expressed universally in terms of the pion form factor. The same representation is then derived starting from the Lellouch-L\"uscher-Meyer expression for the spectral decomposition of the correlator. The results may prove useful for controlling the $L \to \infty$ extrapolation of smeared spectral densities, in particular by defining a scaling regime in which the finite-volume effects are dominated by the leading terms in a large $L$ expansion and thus can be reliably estimated. To illustrate this point, we also present numerical estimates based on various kernels and models of particle interactions. Despite focusing on the vector channel, our derivation defines a general framework applicable to other cases as well.
item.dc:creator: Francesca A. Bresciani, Mattia Bruno, Maxwell T. Hansen

item.title: Scalar diquark mass and quark--diquark potential from lattice QCD using the potential method with a static quark
item.description: arXiv:2606.19840v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the scalar diquark mass and the quark--diquark potential by applying a HAL QCD-inspired potential method to a baryonic system composed of a scalar diquark and a static quark. The diquark mass is determined self-consistently by requiring that the p-wave baryonic spectrum obtained from two-point correlators be reproduced within the potential framework. Numerical calculations are performed using $2+1$ flavor QCD gauge configurations generated by the PACS-CS Collaboration on a $L^{3} \times T = 32^{3} \times 64$ lattice with $a^{-1} \approx 2.176$ GeV and the pion mass, $m_{\pi} \approx 702$ MeV. From the analysis, we obtain a scalar diquark mass which is close to the na\"{\i}ve constituent quark estimate $ (2/3)m_{N}$, together with a quark--diquark potential of the Cornell type (Coulomb + linear). The string tension extracted from the quark--diquark potential agrees within approximately 5% with that obtained from the static quark--antiquark potential (Wilson Loop).
item.dc:creator: Kai-Wen Kelvin-Lee, Noriyoshi Ishii

item.title: The two-flavor Schwinger model at 50: Solving Coleman's puzzles
item.description: arXiv:2605.08042v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In his 1976 paper "More about the massive Schwinger model," Coleman introduced $1+1$-dimensional Quantum Electrodynamics coupled to two charged massive fermions. By applying Abelian bosonization, he elucidated much of the physics of this two-flavor Schwinger model, but he listed three puzzles at the end of his paper. We present new analytical and numerical calculations to solve Coleman's three puzzles and thereby deepen our understanding of this model. These puzzles pertain to the theory with equal fermion masses at $\theta = 0$ and at $\theta = \pi$, as well as the size of isospin-breaking effects when the fermion masses are unequal. For the puzzle at $\theta = \pi$, the solution is related to the structure of the zero-temperature phase diagram arXiv:2305.04437: for equal fermion masses $m$, the model exhibits spontaneous breaking of charge conjugation symmetry and absence of confinement for any value of the gauge coupling $g$, so that there is a smooth interpolation from weak to strong coupling. Using two-loop Renormalization Group and integrability methods, we show that the mass gap behaves as $\sim m e^{-0.111 g^2/m^2}$ in the strong coupling regime $m\ll g$. Our numerical results using the lattice Hamiltonian are in good agreement with this behavior. For the puzzle at $\theta = 0$, the solution is related to a level crossing between two isosinglet particles with different discrete quantum numbers; we demonstrate the necessity of such a crossing by comparing integrability and weak coupling calculations, and we also exhibit the crossing numerically. Finally, we provide a new estimate for the size of isospin-breaking effects caused by different fermion masses at strong coupling.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Cuomo, Ross Dempsey, Andrei Katsevich, Igor R. Klebanov, Ilia V. Kochergin, Silviu S. Pufu, Benjamin T. S{\o}gaard
